questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word ‘Decipher’ from the given sentence.

Many sculptures of our history are like the unravelled path as we cannot garble and there is a lot of work that is yet to be interpreted or translated.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Garble**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The question requires us to find the most appropriate **antonym** (opposite in meaning) of the word **‘Decipher’** from the context provided in the sentence.
 
• **'Decipher'** means to make out the meaning of something that is not immediately obvious, especially to convert from a code, or to discover the meaning of any difficult or illegible writing. (समझना या डिकोड करना).
 
 
• **For example, **"Archaeologists are still trying to decipher the ancient inscriptions found on the cave walls."
 
 
 
• In the given context,** 'Garble'** is the correct antonym as it means to confuse or to mix up something to the extent that its original meaning is obscured or distorted. (गड़बड़ करना या उलझाना).
 
 
• **For example,** "The message was so garbled that I couldn't understand its content."
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2) **Garble**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unravelled **suggests the process of undoing twisted, knitted, or woven threads, but metaphorically, it also refers to solving a mystery or understanding a complex situation. (सुलझाना).
 
• **Interpreted** means to explain the meaning of information, words, or actions, which is actually a synonym of 'Decipher'. (व्याख्या करना).
 
• **Translated** involves converting text or speech from one language to another, also aligning closely with 'Decipher' in terms of unveiling meanings. (अनुवाद करना).

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The shop owners were requested to close the shops by the agitators.

options.text: The agitators request the shop owners to close the shops.
The agitators have requested the shop owners to close the shops.
The agitators are requesting the shop owners to close the shops.
The agitators requested the shop owners to close the shops.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The agitators requested the shop owners to close the shops**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **subject **of the Passive Voice is changed into the **object** of the Active Voice. Also, the **object** of the Passive Voice is changed into the **subject** of the Active Voice.
 
• The **removal** of the **helping verb** and the preposition **'by' **is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.
 
• The Passive voice in this question is in **Past Indefinite**. Thus, the Active voice will also be in **Past Indefinite**.
 
• In Passive voice, the format is: **Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case)**.
 
• Thus, the format of Active voice is: **Subject + V2 + Object.**
 
• For example:
 
 
• The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)
 
• Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)
 
 
 
• The options except (4) don’t follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***The agitators requested the shop owners to close the shops***.

questions.question:
Select the idiom that gives the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase in the following sentence.

Our secretary is always in the mood for an argument. He must __learn to keep quiet__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **To hold his tongue**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'learn to keep quiet'** in the sentence suggests the need for someone to learn to keep quiet or refrain from speaking, especially to avoid arguing or causing conflict.
 
• **'To hold his tongue'** is an idiom that means to refrain from speaking, to keep silent, or to avoid speaking hastily or impulsively. (चुप रहना).
 
 
• For example, "During the heated discussion, John had to remind himself to hold his tongue to avoid making the situation worse."
 
 
 
• This idiom perfectly matches the context provided as the most appropriate meaning for the underlined phrase indicating the need for the secretary to learn to maintain silence in situations where he feels inclined to argue.

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***To hold his tongue***.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **'To go through' **means to undergo or experience a difficult or challenging situation. (से गुजरना).
 
• **'To turn up'** means to arrive at a place, especially unexpectedly or without making a firm arrangement. (प्रकट होना).
 
• **'To take off'** has several meanings, including an aircraft beginning to fly, but in a more colloquial sense, it can mean to suddenly leave, or to start to succeed. (उड़ान भरना) for aircraft or (सफल होना) for success.
